title: Atherosclerotic Morphometry in Pigs
author: Tim Nichols
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7s6hnhe

steps.title: Fix and photograph abdominal aorta
steps.instruction: Open the abdominal aorta longitudinally, immerse‑fix it in 10 % buffered paraformaldehyde, then photograph the opened aorta to record the total surface area and any macroscopically raised lesions for later percent‑surface‑area calculation (method as described for coronary arteries).

steps.title: Segment fixed aorta
steps.instruction: Cut the fixed aorta into 1 cm‑long segments perpendicular to blood flow, spanning from the renal arteries to the origin of the iliac arteries, yielding 10–12 segments per pig.

steps.title: Prepare aortic cross‑sections and stain
steps.instruction: From the proximal half of each 1 cm segment, cut at least three transverse light‑microscopic sections, then stain the sections with Verhoeff‑van Gieson and with hematoxylin‑and‑eosin.

steps.title: Digitize and measure aortic sections
steps.instruction: Capture digital images of each aortic cross‑section, then, in a blinded fashion, use computer‑assisted planimetry (same system as for coronary arteries) to determine intimal plaque area, intimal area as percent of medial area, and percent surface area with raised lesions.

steps.title: Fix heart and coronary arteries
steps.instruction: Fix the harvested heart and attached coronary arteries by immersion in 10 % buffered paraformaldehyde.

steps.title: Section coronary arteries at 1 cm intervals
steps.instruction: Cut transverse sections of each coronary artery perpendicular to flow at 1 cm intervals from the arterial origin, obtaining a total of 19–21 sections per pig (approximately 7 left anterior descending, 8 right coronary, and 4–6 circumflex sections).

steps.title: Stain coronary sections
steps.instruction: Stain the coronary artery sections with Verhoeff‑van Gieson to highlight internal and external elastic laminae; stain adjacent sections with hematoxylin‑and‑eosin to confirm lesion details.

steps.title: Capture coronary images
steps.instruction: Digitize each coronary cross‑section using a Nikon Microphot‑FXA microscope coupled to an Optronics TEC 470 CCD video camera system linked to a Macintosh computer.

steps.title: Measure elastic laminae and lumen
steps.instruction: Using NIH Image software, trace and measure the external elastic lamina (EEL), internal elastic lamina (IEL), and lumen of each section.

steps.title: Calculate atherosclerosis indices
steps.instruction: Compute (1) intimal plaque area = area within IEL − luminal area; (2) % luminal narrowing by intima = (intimal area ÷ area within IEL) × 100; (3) intimal area as % medial area = [intimal area ÷ (area within EEL − area within IEL)] × 100.

steps.title: Record summary statistics and observer consistency
steps.instruction: For each pig group, calculate mean and standard deviation of all measured values for the abdominal aorta and each coronary artery; ensure each slide contains at least three cross‑sections measured by at least two blinded observers, with inter‑ and intra‑observer variability between 4 % and 7 %.
